mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for at least two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during confirmed rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.6%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations that prompt the Fed to signal future rate hikes, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During confirmed high-inflation regimes, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when CPIAUCSL change is ≤ +0.6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a concurrent decline in UNRATE (≥ -0.2 percentage points) signals a strengthening labor market without wage inflation, which boosts consumer confidence and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by ≥ 0.2 percentage points
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening without wage inflation
failure_condition: In labor-strong regimes, the 60-day SPX forward return is not positive (median negative) when the PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction pattern is absent.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 of at least 5% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level (classic 'double-dip' pattern) predicts a temporary boost in business confidence and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 drops at least 5% in two consecutive months and then rises above the lower of those two months in the third month
failure_condition: During uncertainty-resolution periods, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when the GDPC1 double-dip pattern is not observed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly contraction in INDPRO (≥ -8%) suggests weakening business activity and rising supply-side risks, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 8% in a single month
failure_condition: During supply-side contraction, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines < -8%.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.0% for three consecutive months, it signals accommodative policy persistence that lowers real rates and supports higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In prolonged accommodation regimes, the 20-day forward return is not positive (median ≤ 0) when FEDFUNDS ≥ 1.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in HOUST (≥ +15%) followed by a sustained decline (≥ -10%) over the next two months indicates a sharp rotation in inventory, which can precede a rebound in consumer spending and yield positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 15% in one month and then falls by at least 10% in the following two months
failure_condition: During inventory cycle transitions, the 60-day forward return is not positive when the HOUST spike-to-trough pattern is absent.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by at least 20% in two consecutive months while UNRATE remains stable or rises, it signals deteriorating corporate credit conditions that suppress growth expectations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥ 20% in two consecutive months and UNRATE does not decline
failure_condition: In credit-stress regimes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (median ≥ 0) when RSAFS declines < 20% or UNRATE declines as well.
